I farm the way I know will keep my 8 mu steady and manageable for my family. I have been doing wheat-maize rotation for many years, and with some family members working off-farm, I cannot choose a system that needs too much labor at the wrong time. I will keep all 8 mu in winter wheat followed by summer maize, because that fits my land, my experience, and my irrigation conditions. For wheat, I will use improved seed because I want better stand and more stable yield than old seed, but I will not make the management too complicated. I will apply a moderate amount of nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium, give irrigation at the key stages, and use rotary tillage because it is practical and saves effort on my small farm. For maize, I will use hybrid seed because that is what I would trust for yield in summer. I will fertilize a bit more heavily on nitrogen than wheat, irrigate when summer rain is not enough, and keep pesticide use limited to what is needed. My goal is not the highest possible yield, but a reliable harvest with work and input levels I can actually handle.
